findings: All thirteen canonical Porter-Duff/plus modes use a provider-independent factor table and explicit D3D color/alpha factor matching. Noncanonical factor pairs remain rejected.

ABI 11 carries nine additional modes. Tests preserve ABI 1-10, roundtrip uniform/general texture/resource packets, and reject mismatched versions, unknown modes, missing marker/enable, overlapping older mask flags and unsupported texture specializations.
The captured destination-over draw now matches scalar, CPU and NPU output exactly. The three-output distinction is checked before a new live desktop trial.
The initial v129 clean build rejects a signed/unsigned comparison warning; the factor table now uses the native blend enum type.

The v130 CPU suites and captured CPU/NPU replay pass, but its generalized graph regresses destination-out on NPU. v131 omits zero terms, resolving that regression and passing modes 0-9, but additive mode returns zero instead of byte 224. v132 also removes the multiplication by one in the destination term; its isolated tests precede the final clean v133 build. These are observed graph workarounds, not a proven compiler root cause.
Broader desktop operations, usable input, physical scanout and Tahoma benefit remain unproven.
